title: Surat: attention
hook: surat is attention; where attention goes, life follows

segments.voice: Yesterday, man, the mind, and the Guru speaking to it: O my mind. Your line: befriend the mind.

A pot of milk on the stove. You're watching it, and it sits there doing nothing, the way milk does. Your phone buzzes. You glance down, answer one message, maybe two. When you look up, the milk has climbed the pot and is pouring over onto the flame. Nothing about the milk changed. Nothing about the stove changed. The only thing that moved was where you were looking. Yesterday was the mind. Today is the part of the mind that decides where to look.
screen: `MILK ON THE STOVE.` → `ONE GLANCE AT THE PHONE.` → `ONLY YOUR LOOKING MOVED.`

segments.voice: Surat, said like soo-rut, is attention or awareness in the Granth: the inner faculty that goes out toward something and stays with it. If the man is the whole restless inner self, surat is its gaze. Early in the Japji, Guru Nanak gives a run of stanzas that each begin with one word, suniai, by listening. By listening, he says, sorrow and wrongdoing fall away; by listening, a person comes to know the earth and the heavens. That isn't casual hearing with one ear on the phone. It's attention, whole and turned toward the Word. And attention can be trained. In the realm of effort, which we met three days back, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: there, surat is shaped, along with understanding, mind and intellect. Shaped, the way a potter shapes clay or a smith shapes metal. So attention isn't a fixed amount you were born with. It can be worked on, slowly, like a muscle or a craft. Where attention goes, life follows. A day isn't really made of hours. It's made of what you looked at during them. The milk on the stove is a small picture of a large truth: a marriage, a friendship, a child, a prayer, all boil over or go cold depending on where the surat sits. Sikh practice keeps returning the surat to the Name, again and again, gently. Attention is life.
screen: `SURAT: THE MIND'S GAZE.` · `SUNIAI: BY LISTENING.` · `IN THE REALM OF EFFORT, SURAT IS SHAPED.` · `WHERE ATTENTION GOES, LIFE FOLLOWS.` · then, large: `ATTENTION IS LIFE.`

segments.voice: Put your whole surat on the air coming in at the nose, cool, and going out, warm; that's the whole job. When attention slides off to a list or a worry, notice where it went, without a lecture, and bring it back the way you'd turn back to the stove. If you pray, let Waheguru ride on the breath.
Surat. Attention, awareness: the mind's gaze, which the Japji says is shaped in the realm of effort. Today's word.
Your line: attention is life. The milk only boils over when you look away. That's day one thousand three hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: Sikhs speak of joining surat, attention, to the Guru's Word, and practices like listening to kirtan and repeating the Name are ways of returning wandering attention to the One.
